_comment: A routed squadron at the edge of its pursuer's reach gets clear of it (#1801, re-judged for #1949). A brittle player squadron (16 Cavalry at morale 0.5) stands on open ground; an enemy Infantry block (40 men, 10 files) 210 wu to its east, facing it, charges it with no player input. The squadron turns to meet it, fights from about tick 226 and routs at tick 325 still in contact on seeds 0 to 4 (the setup checks read ROUTING at 325 and 326 and in contact at 326). Each routed man then runs on his own from the infantry he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), and the infantry follows in its ranks. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch: the squadron is still in contact at tick 430, out of it from tick 448 at the latest and still out of it at tick 476 (pinned), and its men's centroid runs north-east from (542.7 to 542.9, 982.0 to 982.3) at the rout to (657.0 to 671.7, 903.7 to 907.4) at tick 560, where it is still routing and the clip ends. #1801 and #1913 pinned the squadron's couple() anchor at ticks 430, 436, 442 and 448 ((561.09, 955.4) to (562.91, 942.22), tol 3.0 wu) to guard against that anchor switching between the front ranks and the whole block at the edge of the pursuer's reach. The bottom-up flight (#1949) removed the anchor: a routed unit's position is the centroid of its men. So those four pins are retired, and the contact pin, which fails for a rout that stays in the pursuer's reach, carries the clip's claim.

follow_error.reason: follow_error, the relational successor of shape_residual, reads uid1 44.83 against 13.5 on this tree (dense 2-tick FULL dump, Windows, seed 0, measured 2026-11-13); the slot-based shape_residual this exemption was written against read uid1 37.3. Original reason: The infantry pursuer (uid 1) deforms while it follows the router at the edge of melee range, from about tick 440 to the clip's end, and the deformation is pre-existing (36.0 on main 45a9bb85 on the first sample set). Measured 2026-11-10 on aef5b476, seeds 0 to 4, every exemption removed. On dense 2-tick FULL dumps over ticks 2 to 600 the verdict FAILS on every seed: worst 37.3, 35.2, 40.1, 35.1 and 37.7 against the 13.5 threshold. On the clip's own declared ticks the samples are too sparse to sustain the failure, so the scan reads the exemption as STALE there (the worst reads 0, 33.9, 39.8, 35.1 and 37.5 on seeds 0 to 4, all passing). Kept because the dense dumps fail on every seed. Tracked as #1824.
